title: Mountain Ridge student honored by classmates, teachers for saving dad's life with CPR

Anna Elggrin was in for a big surprise when she walked into her student body government class at Mountain Ridge High School. Anna Elggrin was in for a big surprise when she walked into her student body government class at Mountain Ridge High School.
She was secretly being honored by classmates, teachers, and family for doing something amazing: she saved the life of her father, Brandon.
“She apparently jumped right in she literally pulled me off the couch, dragged me to the floor, and started CPR until the paramedics got there," Brandon said. "Here I am because of her. To say I love my daughter is an understatement; she is absolutely my hero. ”Matt Birch and his company, “Advanced CPR Training,” had recently taught Anna’s class how to perform CPR.
“We do 3,200 high schools and junior high schools from Salt Lake to Payson, and last year we taught 11,665 students how to do CPR," Matt said. "She didn’t panic; she remembered the training and got to work. " “I hung up with my mom and immediately called 911," Anna said. " I dragged him onto the hardwood floor, and I’m not really a strong girl I don’t know what happened.
I guess it was adrenaline. It’s like I turned into the Hulk. I was like Super Woman. ”“I was working so hard on his chest, and then he made a noise, and he pushed my hands away.
I think I was hurting his ribs," Anna said. Brandon agreed. He said, "I woke up three days later, and it felt like a mule had kicked me right in the chest, but I was alive. ”“When you hear a story like this, it really encourages us and gives us a reason to keep doing this work," Shani said.
"Teach as many people as possible because someday that person in trouble might be me. ” Anna received a gift basket during the celebration, and Matt Birch is nominating Anna for a “Heartfelt Hero” award from the American Heart Association.
“Anna, the fact that you saved your dad’s life is amazing. Please accept this 'Pay It Forward' gift on behalf of MACU and or friends at KUTV," Steve Wright with Mountain America Credit Union said. Anna’s dad summed it up nicely. He said, “Everyone should take that class, and most who do may never have to use it, but it’s nice to have it in your back pocket just in case.
